newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-StorageTek CEO sees good margins.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-StorageTek CEO sees good margins.

text.p: Storage Technology Corp's Chief Financial Officer, David Lacey, said on Thursday he expects gross margins for 1997 to be "bouncing around 40 percent," athough the figure could dip below that level in the normally weaker first quarter.
Gross margins in the fourth quarter of 1996 stood at 40.9 percent and for all of 1996 were at 41.52 percent, compared with year-earlier levels in the 35-36 percent range, he said.
Lacey, who spoke with Reuters after addressing analysts about the company's record fourth-quarter results, also said he expects spending on research and development to rise.

Lacey said he cautioned the analysts that if the company's sales from an original equipment manufacture (OEM) agreement with International Business Machines Corp continue strong than gross margins could also see some pressure.

He explained that margins on an OEM contract tend to be lower, but that if such sales did increase it would help Storage Technology's profit picture. "Our operating profit would go up. That's good in the end," he said.
The OEM contract with IBM has been a boon to Storage Technology, Lacey said.
